summary: HTTP/2 flow-control window exhaustion causes SSE/WebSocket stream to stall mid-generation
description: Issue summary: Customer reports chat streaming sessions abruptly stall ~2-3KB into the response. The LLM continues generating (tokens advance in runtime traces) but client receives no further SSE chunks and the HTTP/2 stream remains open until client reconnect. Impact: customers experience partial responses and delayed reconnection workarounds; higher-cost repeated requests. Environment: prod (us-east-1), requests from enterprise dedicated account using dedicated tenancy and edge ingress via our managed envoy fleet. Observed patterns: stalls correlate with responses that emit many small token frames (lots of short chunks), and with clients behind corporate proxies. This is not a model decoder crash — tokens complete on the worker but are not delivered to the client due to transport-layer flow control behaviour.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a small-chat prompt that causes many short tokens (e.g., tables/markdown with many small emits).
2) From a client that negotiates HTTP/2 (curl --http2 -N), open SSE streaming request against /v1/chat/stream with streaming=true and observe bytes delivered.
3) Observe that ~2-3KB of content arrives then no further bytes for >15s while backend still shows active token generation.
4) Reconnect the stream: subsequent connection often resumes generation with duplicate or truncated content depending on client resume logic.
logs: edge-envoy: stream_id=1345 stalled: no WINDOW_UPDATE from downstream for 18s; upstream keepalive OK
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: client-side read blocking or corporate proxy coalescing. Reproduced with curl without corporate proxy: no stall. Reproduced when routing through corporate-like proxy that enforces small initial window sizes.
Envoy debug shows the HTTP/2 connection's flow-control window on the downstream side hitting zero and not receiving WINDOW_UPDATE until client sends additional frames or reconnects.
Serving runtime continues generating tokens and writes to upstream connection successfully; bytes are buffered in envoy connection and not forwarded due to exhausted window.
A quick experiment increasing the initial_window_size and stream_window_size on an envoy canary removed the stall in 90% of test cases.
comments: Lina Patel (Support): Customer first reported at 2026-03-10 07:10 UTC — saw stall mid-response when streaming large markdown output.

Marco Diaz (SRE): Collected debug logs; observed WINDOW_UPDATE starvation on downstream HTTP/2 connections. Adding periodic empty chunk keepalive might mitigate but root cause is low downstream window handling.
Cameron Lee (Customer): Confirmed reproduces when routing through corporate Zscaler; direct connections to Redwood do not stall.
Marco Diaz (SRE): Deployed ingress envoy canary with increased initial stream window and aggressive WINDOW_UPDATE policy (PR: gh/infra/5521). Monitoring for regressions.
Lina Patel (Support): Customer verified after canary deploy — streaming resumed without stalls in their test harness. Marking resolved for now; recommend follow-up hardening.
Product Ops: File follow-up to consider default window tuning and add server-side periodic keepalive churn to avoid stalls for small-chunk-heavy streams.
resolution: Canary change applied to ingress envoy: increased HTTP/2 initial_window_size and enabled more frequent WINDOW_UPDATE flushes for streaming routes (gh/infra/5521). Customer confirmed no stalls after canary; change rolled to production 2026-03-11 03:20 UTC. Follow-up: task created to add periodic zero-byte keepalive chunk from gateway for SSE streams and add tests for low-window proxies.
